name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterized PWM controller with synchronous active-low reset, enable-controlled counter progression, programmable period wrap, and duty-cycle-based PWM output generation.

fixed_assumptions: All sequential state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
counter_value and pwm_out are registered/synchronous outputs derived from the internal counter state.
period is interpreted as an inclusive terminal count: when the counter reaches period, it resets to zero on the next active counting clock.
If duty_cycle is zero, pwm_out remains low; if duty_cycle exceeds the current counter_value range, pwm_out follows the less-than comparison per the registered counter value.

feature_contracts.description: Asserting reset_n low clears all sequential state and forces PWM output low.
With reset released and enable high, the counter increments on successive clocks until wrap conditions apply.
When the counter reaches the programmed period, it resets to zero on the next enabled clock.
PWM output is high whenever counter_value is strictly less than duty_cycle.
PWM output is low when counter_value is greater than or equal to duty_cycle.
When enable is low, the counter does not advance.

functionality: Implements a configurable pulse-width modulation generator. When enable is asserted, an internal 8-bit counter advances by one on each rising edge of clk. The counter resets to zero synchronously when it reaches the configured period value, thereby creating a repeating PWM frame. The output pwm_out is asserted whenever the current counter value is strictly less than duty_cycle, and deasserted otherwise. All state elements initialize to zero under active-low reset_n.
responsibilities: Generate a PWM waveform using a less-than comparison between counter value and duty cycle.
Honor enable gating so that the counter only advances when enable is high.
Wrap the counter to zero at the programmed period terminal count.
Provide the current counter value as an observable output.
Apply a deterministic all-zero reset state on reset_n low.
reset_behavior: When reset_n is low, the internal counter state and all registered outputs are reset to zero. While reset_n remains low, pwm_out shall be low and counter_value shall read as zero. Deassertion of reset_n returns the controller to normal synchronous operation on the next rising clock edge.
behavior_rules: The counter updates only on rising edges of clk.
When enable is low, the counter retains its current value.
When enable is high and the counter value is less than period, the counter increments by one on the next clock.
When enable is high and the counter value reaches period, the counter returns to zero on the next clock.
pwm_out is high only when counter_value is strictly less than duty_cycle.
counter_value must reflect the internal counter state and be stable between clock edges except for reset assertion effects.
The design must be synthesizable in standard SystemVerilog and avoid inferred latches or combinational feedback loops.
